_comment: Hand-written author + blurb per book, keyed by normalized title (lowercase, apostrophes removed, alphanumerics only). build-book-club.py reads this and preserves it across rebuilds. Add an entry for a new book to give it a real author/blurb; otherwise the script falls back to an Open Library description or a placeholder. Cover art is looked up automatically by title from Open Library and stored under assets/book-club/<slug>.jpg.

mynameisasherlev.author: Chaim Potok
mynameisasherlev.blurb: A Hasidic boy in postwar Brooklyn is born with a gift for painting that his faith and his father cannot hold. Chaim Potok's quiet, aching novel about the cost of a calling.

extremelyloudincrediblyclose.author: Jonathan Safran Foer
extremelyloudincrediblyclose.blurb: Nine-year-old Oskar Schell searches all five boroughs of New York for the lock that matches a key his father left behind on 9/11. Inventive, funny, and heartbreaking.

janeeyre.author: Charlotte Brontë
janeeyre.blurb: An orphaned, plain, penniless governess who refuses to be anyone's but her own. Charlotte Brontë's 1847 classic still burns with conscience, temper, and love.

flowersforalgernon.author: Daniel Keyes
flowersforalgernon.blurb: An experimental surgery makes Charlie Gordon a genius, and a lab mouse named Algernon shows him exactly where the road leads. Told in Charlie's own progress reports.

leadershipandselfdeception.author: The Arbinger Institute
leadershipandselfdeception.blurb: A business parable about the 'box' we climb into the moment we betray what we know is right, and how self-deception quietly wrecks the people around us.

manssearchformeaning.author: Viktor E. Frankl
manssearchformeaning.blurb: A psychiatrist survives the concentration camps and builds a philosophy from what he saw there: that meaning, not comfort, is what keeps a person alive.

lordoftheflies.author: William Golding
lordoftheflies.blurb: Schoolboys stranded on an island build a society and then take it apart. Golding's Nobel-winning parable of the savage waiting under the civilized skin.

frankenstein.author: Mary Shelley
frankenstein.blurb: Mary Shelley was eighteen when she imagined a creature that asks its maker the oldest question there is: why give me life only to abandon me? The original science-fiction novel.

theterminallist.author: Jack Carr
theterminallist.blurb: A Navy SEAL comes home to find his men and his family gone and the record rewritten to blame him. He starts a list of the names responsible and works his way down it.
